position: Reform Conservation Programs (Reform NRCS wetlands and erodible land compliance and appeals)
proposal: The Mandate recommends removing NRCS authority to prescribe specific practices on a farm as a condition of eligibility for USDA programs, and instead requiring a general best-practices plan that a county Soil and Water Conservation District could approve. It also calls for reform of the compliance appeals process and, at a minimum, support for legislation shifting more power over highly erodible land and wetland conservation to states and possibly local districts.

status_summary: No change to NRCS authority to prescribe farm practices, no shift to plans approved by Soil and Water Conservation Districts, and no Administration support for legislation moving compliance authority to states was found. S. 1495, the NRCS Wetland Compliance and Appeals Reform Act, introduced 2025-04-10 and referred to the Senate Agriculture Committee with no later action, would require USDA to prove violations by clear and convincing evidence, change wetland appeals and create state oversight committees of active farmers and ranchers, which matches the appeals part of the recommendation. USDA's interim rule of 2026-07-29 (91 FR 47779), issued after a 2024 district court decision vacated a 2020 NRCS rule, treats wetland determinations issued since 1990-11-28 as certified when the producer was notified with appeal rights and states that NRCS has no independent authority to question prior certified determinations on agricultural land, but it leaves practice requirements, appeal procedures and state or district roles unchanged. In CTM Holdings v. USDA the Northern District of Iowa granted summary judgment to USDA on 2025-05-29, holding Swampbuster a valid spending-power condition and dismissing the claims with prejudice.

timeline.event: S. 1495, the NRCS Wetland Compliance and Appeals Reform Act, was introduced by Sen. Rounds and referred to the Agriculture Committee; it addresses burden of proof, wetland appeals, state oversight committees and a ban on new permanent NRCS easements.

The Northern District of Iowa granted summary judgment to USDA and intervenors in CTM Holdings v. USDA, holding Swampbuster a valid condition on federal benefits under the spending power, finding no final agency action or standing for the APA claims and unexhausted regulatory claims, and dismissing all claims with prejudice.

The interim rule responds to National Wildlife Federation v.
